name: Jamie Hamilton
life: “I still remember spelling a nickname the way a man actually said it.” People around Maré Coffee know Jamie by a small Tuesday habit. Jamie likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I make the retirement plaques. One misspelling on the old time sheets has become a nickname they both want on the brass.
appearance: Jamie has short black hair swept back, one cheek that creases before the other, and a favorite piece of clothing, a red windbreaker. It usually goes with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. When somebody else has the floor, Jamie turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Jamie can be lavish with time and quite careful with cash. A free afternoon is sometimes the biggest gift Jamie can afford to give, and family knows to take it seriously.
agenda: To put the familiar spellings on the plaques.
family: Parker Valdez is Jamie’s stepsibling. Jamie is free to hang up first. Parker makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The ladder crossing*, Parker says, “I was late for an interview. I described the crossing when they asked how I handle delays.”
connections: Marcel Easton. The person making the plaque brings it to the room where the kettle and the crew actually are.

reactions.situation: The two old workers are offered separate farewell days
reactions.response: Jamie asks each worker separately what kind of last day they want.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Jamie stays where the child can see the shop door and asks the neighboring counter to help find the adult expected there.

reactions.situation: If invited to an expensive outing
reactions.response: Jamie suggests meeting afterward and explains why without asking the others to abandon their plans.
